subject: Customer handoff: k6 scripts, IP allowlist & latency gates
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara@optimo.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@optimo.ai>
Date: 2028-06-10T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's SLO sync

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap from our side and a couple of asks before we hand off to our SREs for the customer-led run: 

Summary of what we need you to validate for the June run:
- Confirm that the model variant we'll be using (redwood/gptx-lite-2) can meet our latency gate: p99 <= 180ms for 32-token responses under baseline concurrency.
- Throughput target: sustain 220 requests/sec for the scripted ramp (single-region).
- Streaming: we have a streaming-heavy flow (server-sent events) that maintains 8 concurrent streams per user — can you confirm that session KV cache behavior will be preserved across bursts?
- We'll provide k6 scripts and IP ranges for allowlist. We need a test account + short-lived API key and guidance on max tokens and rate-limit headers so our scripts can back off.

Attached: our initial k6 bundle (we'll send the full tar in the next email).

High level ask: can Redwood run a validation pass against these SLO lines and confirm any recommended model/config changes (batching, quantization profile, or a slightly higher-tier instance) before we schedule the customer-led window?

Thanks — happy to jump back on a 20m call if it's easier.

--
Sara Lim
Head of Platform Engineering | Optimo AI
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara@optimo.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-11T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer handoff: k6 scripts, IP allowlist & latency gates

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Quick post-call recap and concrete next steps from Redwood: 

What we heard (SLO/behavior):
- p99 latency target: <= 180ms for ~32-token responses (single-region).
- Throughput: target sustained 220 rps with a controlled ramp; short spike tolerance to ~350 rps for 2m bursts.
- Streaming: ~8 concurrent SSE streams/user; preserve KV cache per-session across bursts — we will confirm whether your session affinity requires sticky routing.

Redwood validation plan (what we'll do before your customer-led window):
1) Internal smoke run (we'll execute the k6 bundle you send) to detect immediate resource mismatches (batching thresholds, KV hot shards).
2) Profile pass: measure p50/p95/p99 and token-based unit cost; if p99 exceeds 180ms we will propose one of: a) bump to a larger instance, b) adjust batching window to favor latency, or c) enable a lower-precision quantization profile for faster kernel paths.
3) Streaming probe: replicate 8-concurrency SSE pattern with long-lived connections to validate KV cache and connection re-use.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Sara / Optimo: attach full k6 tarball + any environment variables and the exact request pacing file (ETA: sending today).
- Redwood (Monica): provide IP allowlist template and requested CIDR(s) to feed to your networking team (attached). ETA: today EOD.
- Redwood (Karthik): prep a test API key with scope limited to the test model + short TTL, and a dedicated test endpoint in us-west-2. ETA: 2028-06-12 11:00 PDT.
- Both: agree test window. Proposed customer-led window: 2028-06-19 10:00-14:00 PDT (4h block). If that doesn't work, propose alternate 2028-06-21 08:00-12:00 PDT.

Attachments: redwood-allowlist-template.csv, slo-targets-preview.pdf (preview of the gates we'll try to validate).

Notes on config knobs we may adjust during validation: batching thresholds, max concurrent KV caches per worker, streaming connection pool size, and quantization profile. We'll document any recommended change in a short runbook so your SREs can reproduce.

If it helps, I'll loop in our on-call infra engineer for the smoke run and the runbook handoff once we have scripts.

Thanks — we'll start on the smoke pass as soon as we receive the full artifacts.

--
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara@optimo.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer handoff: k6 scripts, IP allowlist & latency gates

Looping in infra/ops context and a couple of quick engine notes.

Monica — I'll provision the short-lived test API key and a dedicated test endpoint in us-west-2. Note on routing: for streaming-heavy workloads we recommend reserving sticky routing (session affinity) for the session tokens used by the SSE flows; without affinity you can see KV cache misses on reconnect and latency amplification.

Sara — technical notes for your SREs:
- IP allowlist: we'll accept CIDR blocks; please use the redwood-allowlist-template.csv we attached with your external ranges filled in.
- Max tokens: the test key will have a default max_tokens=512; if you need higher for the scripts call it out and we'll widen (short TTL test only).
- Rate-limit headers: we'll emit X-Redwood-RateLimit-Limit and X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining; k6 can read these for client-side backoff.
- Observability: we'll share trace ids and a short tracing hook (one-line) to include in headers so we can map k6 sessions to traces quickly.

I'll post the test key and endpoint as a secure link (DocuSign-style token) to Sara's team once provisioned. ETA as Monica listed: 2028-06-12 11:00 PDT.

Regards,
Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Customer handoff: k6 scripts, IP allowlist & latency gates

Monica / Karthik — thanks, this looks great. Confirming the customer-led window: 2028-06-19 10:00-14:00 PDT is good for us.

We attached the full k6 bundle in this reply (optimo-k6-scripts-v1.tar.gz) — contains:
- scripts/streaming.sjs (SSE flow)
- scripts/generate-load.js (ramp & pacing)
- env/prod-like.env (redacted)
- pacing/220rps-profile.json

IP ranges for allowlist (filled into your CSV):
- 34.201.0.0/16
- 52.24.128.0/18

Test account details (short-lived key to follow from Karthik):
- test-user: optimo_test@optimo.ai
- desired TTL: 8 hours

A couple of observations from our local dry runs (for your reference):
- On our laptop-scale dry runs p99 sits around 140-150ms for 32-token responses with no batching; however when we enable batching (batch window 10ms) p99 moved to ~210ms. We suspect batching knobs will be critical for hitting your p99 goal.
- Streaming stability looks fine for 8 concurrent streams per session, but reconnects under burst cause a small jump in tail latency.

Please let us know when Karthik posts the test key link and any small config flags you want us to set in the env file for the run. We'll be on standby for the smoke run and can push updated scripts rapidly if you recommend changes.

Attachments: optimo-k6-scripts-v1.tar.gz

--
Sara Lim
Head of Platform Engineering | Optimo AI
